page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a marginal note in the right margin beside the verse paragraph; signature and catchword at the foot. Running head at top with page number.

main_text.p: bus,quæ in historia animalium & plantarum [illegible, ~10 letters] tradi solent. Itaque etiam iftorum ordinum creaturas,prouidentiæ uel eam ob cauffam fubijcimus, ut ipsi quoque difcamus omnem curam noftrã conijcere in Dominum, cui nos & res nostræ præcipuè curæ sunt.
main_text.head: VERSUS VIII.

p.i: Fuit verò oriente Sole, præparavit Deus ventum orientalem vehementem, & per-cussit Sol caput Iona, qui astuabat, petivitq; animæ suæ ut moreretur, & dixit: Melior est mors mihi quàm vita mea.

main_text.head: THESIS.
main_text.p: Neque verò vel corporis dolores & morbi, vel animi ægritudo, eò usque nos adducere debent, ut molestiæ omnis se-mel finiendæ gratia, fatalem vitæ nostræ periodum abbreviari velimus.

Etenim, sententia Iacobi Apostoli, pro summo gaudio nobis ducendū est, quoties in tentationes varias inciderimus: probationem enim fidei nostræ parit pa-tientia, quę & perfectum opus habet: Iac. 1.2.3. Ac cum nostræ cum Christo συμμορφώσως [?] pars aliqua sit, mortificatio nostra

page.notes: Greek word at the start of the first line (after "plantarum") is not legible on the scan; left as illegible. The Greek word after "Christo" (apparently συμμορφώσως) is doubtful and marked [?]. Marginal note "Lectio 67." is partly ambiguous in its numeral. Printed "Solcaput" runs two words together as printed. Line-end hyphens in "per-cussit", "se-mel" and "pa-tientia" are printed and kept. Page signature "A 4" and catchword "per" are at the foot.
